archetype.name: Dual-Threat (goal-line hammer)
archetype.definition: A big-armed passer who wins with vertical and intermediate throws, extends plays with his legs, and serves as the Bills' short-yardage and red-zone runner, which is where most of his touchdowns now come from.

report.headline: Efficient big-play passer, padded by a rushing-TD pace that can't hold
report.take:
Allen is the same player he has been since 2020. He throws aggressively downfield, runs more than almost any quarterback, and carries a turnover tax. His 0.265 EPA per dropback ranks 10th and his 8.73 yards per attempt ranks 5th. That passing efficiency is real and in line with a career where he has finished top-10 in EPA per play five times. The fantasy line, first among quarterbacks at 28.1 points a game, leans heavily on seven rushing touchdowns in four games. Five of those came on designed runs that average just 2.05 yards a carry. He is the Bills' goal-line back, a real role that will keep paying. A touchdown in every game, though, is a pace no quarterback sustains.

The passing value is concentrated in the air. On 27 intermediate throws he has a 74% success rate and a +19.5 CPOE. On 21 deep attempts he has 1.11 EPA per play and four of his six passing touchdowns. Short and behind-the-line work is ordinary to poor: screens and swing passes sit at -0.34 EPA. That profile is great when defenses give up chunks and fragile when they don't.

The game log shows the split clearly. Against Houston and Detroit, now the 25th- and 32nd-ranked defenses, he produced +14.5 and +15.0 passing EPA. Against the Chargers (11th) and Patriots (12th) he managed -0.4 and +4.8, including a two-interception, four-sack, 26.9% bad-throw day against LA.

The sacks are the persistent flaw. A third of his pressures end in sacks, 26th of 32, and last season's 40% rate ranked 49th of 64, so this is not a four-game blip. It has become part of who he is. His work under center is nearly worthless (0.009 EPA, five sacks in 50 plays) next to his 0.331 out of shotgun. Seven turnover-worthy plays (three interceptions, four fumbles) fit a career in which he has usually ranked near the bottom in picks. With a defense ranked 29th in EPA behind him, Buffalo will keep needing him to outscore people, and that keeps both the ceiling and the risk high.

strengths.title: Intermediate and deep accuracy
strengths.body: Allen is completing 77.8% between 10 and 19 air yards with a +19.5 CPOE, and the deep ball has produced 1.11 EPA per attempt with four touchdowns. His arm and willingness to drive the ball outside the numbers create this. It has held across his career, though a +19.5 CPOE on 27 throws will come down toward his usual +3 to +6 range.

strengths.title: Legs as a scoring and drive tool
strengths.body: His eight scrambles have gone for 82 yards and six first downs at 1.25 EPA each. His 20 designed runs carry a 65% success rate and five touchdowns despite little yardage. The goal-line role is structural and durable. The touchdown rate, nearly two a game, is the part that regresses.

strengths.title: Third-down conversion
strengths.body: On third down he is converting 48.5% with an average 7.6 yards to go, a +8.9 CPOE, and no interceptions. That is the intermediate game showing up where it matters most, and it fits his career success-rate ranks.

concerns.title: Pressure turns into sacks
concerns.body: A 33.3% pressure-to-sack rate ranks 26th of 32. It follows a 2025 season at 40% (49th), so this is a two-year pattern rather than noise. Some of it is the cost of hunting big plays and running at a 2.94-second time to throw. The under-center split, five sacks in 50 plays and near-zero EPA, suggests the play-action and pro-style looks are where it hurts most.

concerns.title: Production tracks opponent quality
concerns.body: His 29.5 combined passing EPA came against two bottom-eight defenses. He managed 4.4 against the Chargers and Patriots, and the LA game brought two picks and a 26.9% bad-throw rate. A deep-heavy profile is most exposed when a defense takes away explosives.

concerns.title: Red-zone passing has stalled
concerns.body: Inside the 20 his throws have a 20% success rate and a -10.9 CPOE. Buffalo has effectively handed the red zone to his legs. On 18 attempts this is a hint more than a verdict, but it makes his scoring more dependent on rushing touchdowns.

trend.note: His fantasy totals went 35.7 and 40.8 in the first two weeks, then 17.5 and 18.5, with passing EPA following the same path. The drop lines up almost exactly with the move from two bottom defenses to two top-12 units, so it reads as opponent quality more than decline.

nextGame.headline: The NFL's best deep defense meets his deep-ball engine
nextGame.body:
The Rams are built to blunt exactly what has driven Allen's passing. They allow the lowest explosive-pass rate in the league and rank first against deep throws at -0.606 EPA, third on short passes, and fourth in pass EPA overall. Quarterbacks have averaged just 167.5 yards against them, fewest in the NFL. Two things soften the matchup. Their pass rush is ordinary, 23rd in hit rate and 21st in sack rate, which limits his sack problem. And quarterbacks still find the end zone against them at 2 touchdowns a game (21st), which fits Allen's rushing-touchdown profile. Expect a game won on intermediate throws and red-zone runs rather than shots.

Availability helps Buffalo. Starting corner Jaylen Watson (75% of snaps) is out with a dislocated shoulder, and Myles Garrett is on IR. Aaron Donald is listed out with back soreness, though McVay says it is trending toward him playing, which makes him the swing piece for the interior rush. On Allen's side, DJ Moore (shoulder, questionable, not considered long-term) has been productive at 0.319 EPA per target. If Moore sits, more targets go to Keon Coleman, whose 1.05 EPA per target comes from vertical work into the Rams' strength, and to Shakir's low-yield short volume.

keyMatchups.title: Allen's deep ball vs Rams' shell
keyMatchups.body: Four of his six passing touchdowns came on throws of 20-plus air yards, and the Rams lead the league in deep-pass defense. If those shots don't land, his efficiency has to come from the intermediate game.

keyMatchups.title: A soft rush versus his sack habit
keyMatchups.body: LA's 23rd-ranked hit rate, with Garrett out, gives Allen cleaner pockets than usual. Donald's status decides whether the interior holds up. Fewer pressures means fewer of the sacks that have stalled his drives.

keyMatchups.title: Bills' defense forces a shootout
keyMatchups.body: Buffalo's defense ranks 29th in EPA and 28th against the pass. The Rams pass more than expected (6th in pass rate over expectation), so Allen likely needs to keep scoring. That supports volume even against a tough secondary.

nextGame.watch: Whether Buffalo finds 10-to-19-yard windows when the Rams take away the deep ball, or Allen forces shots into their shell.

restOfSeason.body:
The passing core should hold. A top-10 EPA passer with a top-5 yards-per-attempt mark fits his last six seasons. Expect the intermediate CPOE and the deep touchdown rate to cool, and the interception count to drift toward his career norm of roughly 10 to 15 a season. The rushing role is the real fantasy driver. He is Buffalo's goal-line runner and keeps his scrambling value, so rushing touchdowns will keep coming, just closer to one every other game than nearly two a game.

Buffalo's poor defense is the tailwind. It keeps game scripts competitive and his pass volume steady. The sack problem is the drag, a two-season trait that caps his efficiency against good fronts. He stays a top fantasy quarterback with a lower weekly floor against strong pass defenses.
swingFactors: DJ Moore's shoulder and receiver health
Whether the sack rate improves or stays bottom-10

bets.reason: The Rams allow the fewest passing yards to quarterbacks (167.5) and the fewest explosive passes. Allen's yardage leans on deep throws, where LA ranks first. He already averaged just 228.5 yards against the two top-12 defenses he has faced.

That total matches Buffalo's Week 2 game against the 32nd-ranked defense, but the Rams' defense ranks 4th in EPA and their offense is middling (15th). Buffalo's lone under came against the 11th-ranked Chargers, the closest comparison to this defense.

He has scored on the ground in all four games, five times on designed runs, as the Bills' goal-line option. Quarterbacks average 2 total touchdowns a game against LA (21st) even as the yardage dries up. Expect regression in volume, not in the role.

confidence.note: Four games with a clear opponent split; career traits are stable, but the touchdown rates are small-sample.
